Cc: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing & unit-econ alignment — FinApp token targets

Thanks again for the demo today — great to see the ingest/summary flow and the cost sensitivity you called out. Quick recap and two asks so we can put a tight pilot quote together: 

1) Ask: can you confirm the expected monthly token mix (approx) across the three buckets we discussed? Example format in the attached spreadsheet is fine: 
   - Short responses / customer-facing prompts (~< 128 tokens)
   - Multi-turn context & search (~128–512 tokens)
   - Batch analytics / embeddings (~512+ tokens)

2) Ask: high-level budget range and target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for in production (ballpark is fine). You mentioned wanting to be materially below Anthropic/OpenAI for the same latency profile — if you can give a target $/1M (e.g., $X–$Y), that will let us map to reserved vs hosted pricing options.

Why this helps: with rough volumes + target unit price we can recommend either a Hosted pilot (fast to run, higher unit price) or a Dedicated reserved commit (lower $/1M at predictable throughput). I attached a simple token-volume template to populate.

Next steps: if you can drop the sheet back by EOD Monday (Nov 30) I’ll get a pricing playbook and two offer structures to you the next day. If easier, we can take 20 minutes Monday to go line-by-line.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a pilot PO.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

Thanks Karthik — quick answers inline and I attached our rough internal forecast.

- Monthly token mix (est):
  * Short responses / UI prompts: 25M tokens/month
  * Multi-turn context/search: 120M tokens/month
  * Batch analytics (embeddings + long summaries): 55M tokens/month
  Total: ~200M tokens/month to start; 2–3x over 12 months if pilot succeeds.

- Budget / target $/1M tokens:
  * We’re aiming for a target in the $600–$900 per 1M tokens range for initial production. Our procurement team wants to see a path to ~$400–$500 /1M at scale or with a committed reserved plan.

We’re also doing a quick benchmark vs OpenAI/Anthropic and a couple of open-model hosts (self-hosted infra providers). So please include explicit comparisons and where Redwood lands vs those options for the pilot and at 12-month scale.

I’ve attached the forecast: finapp_forecast_v2.xlsx. Happy to jump on 20 min Monday afternoon to review.

—Ava

Subject: Re: Pricing & unit-econ alignment — FinApp token targets

Ava — thanks for the clear forecast (appreciate the spreadsheet). Internal note below for Rishi and Maya, copying you so you can see our recommended approach.

Summary of FinApp ask: ~200M tokens/month; target $600–$900/1M initially with a path to ~$400–$500/1M at scale or under a committed reserved plan.

Prelim pricing approach (high level):
- Pilot (Hosted, 1–2 months): $750 /1M tokens (helps cover burst capacity, monitoring, and quick onboarding) — target quote for PO to start quickly.
- Reserved Commit (6–12 month): tiered discounts that get to $420 /1M at >=1B tokens/month equivalent (commit + performance SLAs).
- Optional: volume-based accelerator credits for the first 90 days to help ramp (one-time credit applied to invoices).

Benchmarks (approx, for comparison only):
- OpenAI (hosted high-capacity tier): typical market references we’re seeing around $900–$1,200 /1M for comparable latency/throughput for chat-style workloads.
- Anthropic (hosted): similar band, often slightly above OpenAI for some models on latency-sensitive configs.
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted infra: wide range; vendors with cheaper unit compute advertise $300–$600 /1M but exclude management, monitoring, and reliability guarantees — and often require heavy ops investment.

Proposal: I’ll prepare two formal offers: a 6-week Hosted pilot priced at $750/1M and a 12-month Reserved Commit structure with breakpoints and a roadmap to $420/1M when volume milestones are met. I’ll include a short comparison table (OpenAI/Anthropic/open hosts) so procurement can see the delta.

Next steps:
- Karhtik: produce formal pilot quote + comparison table (deliverable: Wed, Dec 2)
- Rishi: confirm whether we can include a one-time accelerator credit and the amount (cc'd)
- Maya: include estimated onboarding dates and minimal SRE involvement needed for pilot

If that works I’ll get the quotes over and we can lock a PO cadence.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing & unit-econ alignment — FinApp token targets

Thanks — quick operational notes and green light on structure.

- Accelerator credit: we can offer a $15k usage credit applied within the first 90 days of the pilot to offset initial unit costs (will be reflected as a one-time invoice credit).
- Pilot discount flexibility: we can move the pilot to $700/1M if FinApp agrees to a 90-day pilot PO of at least $25k. That gets us into demonstrable production usage quickly.
- Reserved target path: confirm we can present a plan that hits $420/1M at >=1B tokens/month with quarterly review gates. Finance will accept this if we include clear milestone definitions and an early-exit cap.

Competitor notes for the quote (to include in the comparison appendix):
- OpenAI: depending on model and throughput, procurement references put comparable cost in the $900–$1,100 /1M band for low-latency chat workloads.
- Anthropic: procurement references in similar ranges but sometimes +10–20% premium for certain LLMs.
- Self-hosted options: TCO often looks cheaper at $300–$500 /1M at scale but requires headcount/ops and longer lead time.

I’ll validate final numbers with finance but approve the general structure. Karhtik — you have the go-ahead to send the pilot quote at $700/1M contingent on PO >= $25k and include the $15k credit.

-Rishi
Director, Commercial Sales | Redwood Inference
